summary: This is a Merriam-Webster dictionary entry for the English word "jerk," covering its noun senses (an annoyingly foolish or unlikable person, a sudden quick motion, spasmodic movements, and the weightlifting press overhead), two verb senses (to give a quick arrested push or pull, and to preserve meat in sun-dried strips), along with synonyms, example sentences, etymology and first known uses. Most of the page is site navigation and promotional boilerplate, which is ignored here. The entry was last updated 26 March 2024 and cites an access date of 1 April 2024.
one_line: Merriam-Webster dictionary entry defining the word "jerk" as noun and verb, with senses, synonyms, etymology and usage examples.
key_facts: Merriam-Webster lists "jerk" as a noun with five senses, including an annoyingly stupid or foolish person and a single quick motion of short duration.
The first known use of the noun "jerk" is recorded as 1575, in the meaning defined at sense 2.
The transitive verb "jerk" meaning to give a quick suddenly arrested push, pull, or twist has a first known use in 1589.
The noun sense of "jerk" as weightlifting refers to pushing a weight from shoulder height to a position overhead, the second phase of the clean and jerk.
The verb "jerk" in the sense of preserving meat means to preserve it in long sun-dried slices.
The noun and verb (1) forms of "jerk" are etymologically described as probably an alteration of yerk.
The meat-preserving verb (verb 2) is a back-formation from the entry jerky.
Merriam-Webster gives the example sentence "That jerk can't do anything right."
Merriam-Webster gives the example sentence "The car started with a jerk."
Synonyms for the noun jerk include bastard, boor, cad, louse, rat, and schmuck, among many others.
Synonyms for the verb jerk in the sense of a quick motion include buck, hitch, hoick, jolt, twitch, and yank.
The Kids Definition describes the verb-form etymology as probably an altered form of earlier yerk "to beat or thrash."
The entry's phrases containing jerk include clean and jerk, knee jerk, jerk around, and soda jerk.
The entry was last updated 26 March 2024 with updated example sentences.
